nodes.name: Dragon's blood tree
nodes.desc: An umbrella-crowned tree whose red resin is famous. Goats stop seedlings from growing, so many stands are ageing with little new growth.

nodes.name: Cucumber tree
nodes.desc: The only tree in the gourd family. It stores water in its swollen trunk to survive long dry spells.

nodes.name: Socotra frankincense
nodes.desc: A resin tree found only on Socotra, growing in dry forest and shrubland. It is listed as Endangered.

nodes.name: Socotrine aloe
nodes.desc: A succulent of Socotra's dry slopes and cliffs, with bright flower spikes that offer nectar to birds.

nodes.name: Socotra croton
nodes.desc: A common shrub of Socotra's dry shrubland, part of the low cover that insects and grazers use.

nodes.name: Domestic goat
nodes.desc: Herded across the plateaus for generations. Heavy browsing is a major pressure on Socotra's plants and tree seedlings.

nodes.name: Grasshoppers
nodes.desc: Plant-eating insects of Socotra's shrubland and a food for starlings, lizards and raptors.

nodes.name: Socotra starling
nodes.desc: An island endemic that eats grasshoppers and figs, and the berries of the dragon's blood tree, spreading its seeds.

nodes.name: Socotra sunbird
nodes.desc: An endemic bird that feeds on nectar and insects, and helps pollinate Socotra's flowering plants.

nodes.name: Etruscan shrew
nodes.desc: One of the smallest mammals on Earth and one of Socotra's few native mammals. It hunts small invertebrates.

nodes.name: Socotra rock gecko
nodes.desc: A small rock-dwelling gecko of the island, and one of its many endemic reptiles.

nodes.name: Socotra chameleon
nodes.desc: An island endemic that lives in scrub and along seasonal stream beds, catching insects.

nodes.name: Egyptian vulture
nodes.desc: A small, opportunistic vulture and the most recorded bird in the area. It feeds mainly on carrion and also takes insects and eggs.

nodes.name: Brown-necked raven
nodes.desc: A desert raven that scavenges carcasses and hunts small animals and eggs.

nodes.name: Socotra buzzard
nodes.desc: An island-only buzzard that nests on cliffs and hunts mainly reptiles and large invertebrates.

nodes.name: Feral cat
nodes.desc: An introduced predator that preys on small mammals, birds and lizards, adding pressure to island wildlife.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Strong year-round sun drives plant growth and makes water the main limit on life here.

nodes.name: Monsoon rain
nodes.desc: Seasonal monsoons bring most of the rain, with the northeast monsoon wettest in the highlands.

nodes.name: Highland mist
nodes.desc: Cliffs and mountains catch cloud and mist, creating wetter refuges where many endemic plants grow.

nodes.name: Rocky soil
nodes.desc: Thin, rocky soils hold the nutrients and moisture that plants draw on.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, bacteria and insects that break down dead plants and animals and return nutrients to the soil.
